🧠 Crypto News Brief: A quiet weekend tape keeps Bitcoin pinned near $85K while politics takes the wheel: Trump's $5,000 pledge, Brazil's vote and India's caution set the tone, and a fresh $6M Base exploit keeps DeFi risk in view. 🚨 $6M Drained From Base Vault in Whitelist Exploit An attacker drained about 1,783 wstETH, worth roughly $6 million, from an unnamed DeFi vault on Base on October 4 after adding a newly deployed contract to the vault's whitelist and borrowing Aave Base wstETH through it. Blockaid first flagged about $2.02 million in losses as the attack unfolded; Spot On Chain and PeckShield later traced the full amount to a single attacker address. No official post-mortem has been published yet. Read full story 💵 Trump Repeats $5,000 "Trump Dividend" Pledge President Trump said on October 3 that every adult US citizen would receive $5,000 if Republicans win both the House and Senate in the November midterms, a plan estimated to cost more than $1.2 trillion. Cleveland Fed research found the 2020 $1,200 stimulus checks lifted Bitcoin buy volume by about 3.8%, but Polymarket currently gives a full Republican sweep only around a 7% chance, and funding remains unresolved. More details 🇧🇷 Brazil Votes Today With Crypto Rules at Stake Brazil holds its first-round presidential election on October 4, with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro leading the polls. The country ranks first in Chainalysis' 2026 Global Crypto Adoption Index with an estimated $252.5 billion in activity. Lula's government has tightened oversight, requiring providers to obtain central bank authorization and report large self-custody transfers, while Bolsonaro's official program sets out no dedicated crypto policy. Read more 📊 Ether ETFs Beat Bitcoin ETFs on 2026 Inflows US spot Ether ETFs have drawn about $1.5 billion in net inflows so far in 2026, ahead of the $985 million taken in by spot Bitcoin ETFs, according to SoSoValue data. Bitcoin funds still dominate by size, holding roughly $109 billion versus $18 billion for Ether products, and pulled in $6.3 billion in Q3 alone after about $5 billion of net outflows in the first half.
